title: The Rule You Keep Negotiating

launchpad.outcome: Spot the rule you keep bending, close its loophole, and change rules only in review.
launchpad.missionQuestion: Is this rule protecting me, or am I negotiating with it?

slides.headline: This is the rule you keep negotiating with.
slides.line: A rule you can talk yourself out of is really just optional. Optional rules can’t protect you.

slides.headline: You broke the same rule four days in a row.
slides.line: Each day you had a different reason. Tap each day to see what you told yourself.

steps.label: Monday
steps.sub: You chased an entry, but only “just a little.”

steps.label: Tuesday
steps.sub: You took a third trade because “it was A+.”

steps.label: Wednesday
steps.sub: You moved your stop loss “just this once.”

steps.label: Thursday
steps.sub: You chased again because “this one was different.”

slides.headline: A rule you treat as optional is just decoration.

cards.label: Rule as written
cards.sub: It holds even when you feel emotional.

cards.label: Rule you negotiate
cards.sub: You tell yourself it doesn’t fit this situation.

check.prompt: It’s Thursday and you’re mid-chase. What would you do with the rule?

options.label: Delete it, because it doesn’t fit me
options.feedback: Maybe it really doesn’t fit. But the middle of a chase is the worst moment to judge a rule.

options.label: Flag it and follow it until review
options.feedback: Yes. You change rules in your review, when you’re calm and your journal is open. You never change them mid-session.

slides.headline: Find the escape word hiding in your rule.
slides.line: Small words like “just” give you a way out. Tap each step to see how to close that gap.

steps.label: Cut it out
steps.sub: Rewrite the rule so the live you can’t argue with it.

steps.label: Keep the rule
steps.sub: Follow the rule exactly as written, every single session.

steps.label: Change in review
steps.sub: Change rules only when you’re calm, journal open, never live.

slides.title: Find the escape hatch
slides.weak: I won’t chase unless it looks really good.
critique: Every setup looks really good when you want in.

options.text: I won’t chase unless I’m really sure.
If my planned entry is missed and price moves away, I do not market-enter late. I wait for a new valid setup.

slides.title: Flagged rules wait here
slides.body: In a session, rules are read-only. Flag a rule and it waits here until you review it calmly.

slides.quote: If I have to argue with my rule, the rule already won the argument. I wrote it for this.

slides.prompt: Which rule do you negotiate with most, and what’s your favorite excuse?
slides.modelAnswer: I notice the word I use to escape it. I close the loophole, and if the rule truly needs changing I flag it and change it in review, never mid-session.

takeaways: Change rules in review, never live.
remember: IF A RULE BECOMES OPTIONAL WHEN YOU’RE EMOTIONAL, IT ISN’T PROTECTING YOU.
